backup.procedure: pg_dump -Fc against the application database, run by the platform on its own schedule
backup.restore: pg_restore --no-owner into an empty schema, then roll forward with the app migration command
backup.owner: the platform team that owns the database instance; this app owns the procedure and the rehearsal, not the production schedule or retention window

incidentHooks.name: The application is not serving
incidentHooks.signal: GET /api/health returns a non-2xx status, or does not respond at all, from outside the container

incidentHooks.name: The database is unreachable
incidentHooks.signal: The health endpoint reports 503 and the structured log carries health.database_unreachable entries
incidentHooks.note: The app has no failover logic of its own, so this hook exists to route the incident to Postgres diagnostics rather than to an application investigation.

incidentHooks.name: Ownership boundary breached
incidentHooks.signal: access.forbidden log entries cluster around one actor or one resource, or an audit_logs row records a change by a subject who does not own the task

incidentHooks.name: Session signing key suspected compromised
incidentHooks.signal: Sessions are accepted that the application never issued, or the signing secret is exposed in a log, a backup or a support channel
incidentHooks.note: Rotating the secret is the documented response and invalidates every session at once, which is REQ-016 and REQ-020 in the coverage record — the response is known to be blunt.

incidentHooks.name: Unauthenticated page shell served for an authenticated route
incidentHooks.signal: A request to /tasks without a valid session cookie returns 200 with page HTML instead of a redirect to /login
incidentHooks.note: The edge guard is the only thing standing between an unauthenticated browser and the rendered task list, and it is a separate mechanism from the API-layer check, so it can fail on its own.
